catalog_quote: In general, primary stress falls on the final syllable of nouns, adjectives, and adverbial modifiers. Verb stress is more variable and sometimes falls on the first syllable, as shown in (1.1). In a compound verb, stress usually falls on the final syllable of the nominal element, and not on the inflected verb that follows, as in (1.2). Most grammatical morphemes, such as pronominal agreement clitics, function-marking clitics and adpositions, aspectual morphemes, conjunctions, and modal particles like the conditional tsa and the ability marker tɕi, are not stressed, as in (1.3). The nominalizer -i, diminutive suffix -ik, and negators (na, nist, mo, naj) are exceptions, as they do receive stress, as in (1.4). ... tone_statements.quote: Ударение обычно падает на последний слог: 1) в непроизводных именах — на последний слог основы: [six examples in Latin transcription]; 2) в производных именах, включая причастия и инфинитив, — на суффикс: [six examples]; 3) в личных формах глагола — на исход основы. Сложные слова имеют двойное ударение: основное, падающее на последний слог второй основы, и дополнительное, падающее на последний слог первой основы: [two examples, ‘черноглазый’, ‘носовой платок’]. Безударны личные глагольные показатели, флективные и аналитические (они же — связки): [three examples, ‘я скажу’, ‘мы скажем’, ‘вы скажете’]; большинство односложных послелогов, союзов; предлоги, изафетный показатель, бо́льшая часть энклитических частиц. Фонетический характер ударения не изучен. Тоновые оппозиции не обнаружены.

(2) Deciding source: a 2017 fieldwork-based Leiden dissertation/descriptive grammar, open access, the most recent first-hand description of Sarikoli; but it is a syntax grammar whose stress treatment is a one-page sketch, so verb-stress conditioning is stated loosely. sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Sarikoli language', section 'Stress' (raw wikitext downloaded 2026-09-16), footnoted to Gao Erqiang 1985, Tajikeyu jianzhi, Beijing: Minzu chubanshe.
sources.quote: 'Most words receive stress on the last syllable; however, a minority receive stress on their first syllable. Also, several noun declensions and verb inflections regularly place stress on their first syllable, including the imperative and interrogative.' (an HTML comment adds that Gao lists further verb moods with final stress). Second-hand paraphrase of Gao 1985; matches the record's srule.

sources.citation: Edelman, D. I. & L. R. Dodykhudoeva. 2009. 'The Pamir languages'. In G. Windfuhr (ed.), The Iranian Languages, 773-786. London: Routledge. (already held under sang1344, not downloaded now; read for this compilation)
sources.quote: 'The pattern of stress in nominals tends to be word-final, while that of the verb forms varies according to language, except for obligatory stress on the negative prefix. In general word stress is rather weak and subordinate to a sentence stress.'
sources.locator: section 3.1.3 'Suprasegmental features' (the text); group-level statement for the Pamir languages incl. Sarikoli

sources.note: The only occurrences of 'accent' are in the orthography key, where 'accented' vs 'unaccented' vowels mark vowel quality/length (a as in pawn vs America; i as in machine vs him; u as in rumour vs hund), not word stress. No statement of stress placement, secondary stress, weight, domain, exceptions or tone anywhere in the Sarikoli grammar sketch (printed pp. 20-32), the tales, or the vocabulary. The catalog entry (morphological stress, sec_status 'only in compounds, reduplications or phrases', tone not-mentioned; cited to Kim 2017) is neither confirmed nor contradicted.
